full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner, in short, is that the petitioner challenged the order No. 9 dated 25.7.2005 passed in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 132 of 2005 by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong allowing the decree-holder bank's application and auction schedule fixing 30.8.2005 as the date of auction and publication of the notice of auction of the petitioner's properties   in Chittagong in national "The Dainik Manab Jamin" and local "The Daily Azadi" being contrary to its own decree allowing the petitioner company to pay off the decreetal amount of Tk. 1,33,46,000/- to the decree-holder bank in 4 (four) equal installments within one year from the date of the delivery of judgment, which was delivered on 3.10.2004, being without any lawful authority and of no legal effect and that the order No. 9 suffers from inherent defect in that the time allowing the pensioner company in paying the decreetal amount within one year from the date of the judgment dated 3.10.2004 did not elapse. After hearing the parties High Court Division issued rule and also passed an interim order, i.e. "pending hearing of the rule, let all further proceedings in Artha Rin Adalat Execution Case No. 132 of 2005 pending in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong, and publication of notice of auction as have been published in the national "The Daily Dainik Manab Jamin" on 13.6.2005 stayed till disposal of the rule" and also directed the respondent bank to accord permission for sale of a mortgaged property for liquidating the bank's entire liabilities acquired in the name of Noor Mohammad and five 1 others and so registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Sadar, Chittagong by sale deed No. 2018 dated 19.4.1968 provided the petitioner completes negotiation within   3.10.2005. 

 4. The opposite parties by a letter dated 22.9.2005 asked the petitioner to deposit Tk.1,58,00,000/- (Taka one crore fifty eight lac) only in settlement of its liabilities, which is much more than the total decretal amount and respondent-opposite could not have unilaterally increased the amount of the decree passed by a lawfully constituted Court and furthermore the repayment schedule as passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong, have not elapsed, no interest and or any additional amount far less Tk. 24,22,400/- and the amount arbitrarily added on the decreetal amount of Tk. 1,33,77,000/- and the actions of the opposite parties are in effect in total disregard of the decree of the Artha Rin Adalat and order passed by the High Court Division, which is serious contempt of Court and liable to be penalized for their stubborn, arbitrary and illegal acts. 

 5. The petitioner got their properties by depositing the entire money within time specified by the High Court Division but their case is that the conduct of the respondents in sitting over the matter unduly for long time obstructed the administration of justice and by the demand of excess of the decreetal amount is also a deliberate act of interference with the administration of justice. The further case of the petitioner is that by Annexure-A the respondents virtually frustrated the order of the High Court Division, which was never stated in the application before the Appellate Division at any point of time and dictated the petitioner to do contrary to the order of the High Court Division, which is flagrant violation of the court's order and therefore they should be punished for contempt. 

 8. Mr. M. A. Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that on the face of the writ-petition, which was simply moved by the writ-petitioners with an ulterior motive of creating an illegal pressure against Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited, a private banking company constituted under Companies Act, 1994, the learned Judges of the High Court Division acted without any lawful authority by entertaining such writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution and as such the Rule Nisi as well as the order passed thereunder having had no legal sanction behind it and as such question of violation of such order did not at all arise which warranted for drawing up a lawful legal proceeding of contempt against the petitioners. He further submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division had totally misconceived and misconstrued the scope of their authority under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and thereby misdirected themselves in directing the petitioners, who are the simple employees of the respondent bank, to pay the writ petitioners a sum of Tk. 24,23,000.00 notwithstanding the fact that the Artha Rin Adalat in question passed the decree with interest @ 8% from the date of institution of the suit till its realization and in that view of the matter, the learned Judges of the High Court Division misconstrued the terms of the decree in question in initiating the proceeding   for contempt against the petitioners upon absolutely wrong and baseless information from the writ-petitioners. He lastly submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have failed to take judicial notice of the contents of the letter dated 22-09-2005 issued by the bank, which was annexed by the writ petitioner in the contempt, petition as Annexure-B (1) in finding some fault with the petitioners for realization of a hypnotically excess payment which is not covered by any documentary evidence thereby caused a serious miscarriage of justice which, in public interest, needs to be ratified by the highest judicial forum of the country.
